reports.title: Parents Told To Starve Their Children! Kenya's Shocking Cult Case
reports.description:
A Kenyan preacher told his followers that starving themselves and their children would help them meet Jesus. What followed became one of Kenya's most horrifying cult tragedies.

Paul Mackenzie, founder of Good News International Church, was convicted on October 19, 2026, in connection with the murders of 190 children and one adult.

The case dates back to 2023, when investigators discovered mass graves in Kenya's Shakahola Forest. More than 400 bodies were eventually recovered.

According to investigators, Mackenzie convinced followers to undertake extreme fasting to reach heaven before the end of the world. Children were reportedly ordered to fast first, followed by women and men.

Court proceedings revealed disturbing accounts of starvation, coercion and violence against followers who resisted the group's instructions.

Mackenzie has denied the allegations, but the court found him guilty. Sentencing is scheduled for November 6, 2026.

reports.title: ‘Eight Family Members Gone’: Heartbroken Relative Awaits Mackenzie Ruling
reports.description:
A relative who lost eight family members in Kenya’s Shakahola tragedy is awaiting a court verdict in the case against self-proclaimed pastor Paul Mackenzie. Mackenzie arrived at a Kenyan court as proceedings reached a critical stage in the case linked to the deaths of followers of the Good News International Church. The Shakahola case shocked Kenya and drew international attention to allegations of religious extremism and mass deaths.
